faq.a: ITR-6 is exclusively for companies registered under the Companies Act, that are not claiming exemption under Section 11 of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
Section 11 provides income tax exemptions for income derived from property held under trust for charitable or religious purposes. Entities claiming this exemption do not file ITR-6.
No, individuals cannot use ITR-6. It is specifically designed for companies. Individuals file ITR-1, ITR-2, ITR-3, or ITR-4 depending on their income sources and eligibility.
AY 2026-27 stands for Assessment Year 2026-27. This is the year in which the income earned during the Financial Year 2025-26 (April 1, 2025, to March 31, 2026) is assessed for tax.

faq.q: Is it mandatory to use the Excel utility?
faq.a: The Income Tax Department provides various utilities (Excel, Java) for different ITR forms. While the Excel utility is a popular option, the department also offers other methods like online filing or using third-party software.

faq.q: What if I file ITR-6 late?
faq.a: Late filing of ITR-6 can result in a late filing fee of up to ₹10,000 under Section 234F, interest under Section 234A on unpaid tax, and loss of ability to carry forward certain losses.

faq.q: Where can I download the utility?
faq.a: The ITR-6 Excel utility for AY 2026-27 can be downloaded from the official Income Tax e-Filing portal (incometax.gov.in) under the 'Downloads' section.
